Support

Last updated 15 September 2026 · Effective 15 September 2026

The short version. The game is free and takes no account, so almost every problem has a short answer. Write to support@devildictionary.com and you will get a reply. Nobody will ever ask you for a password, a card number, or a verification code.

1. How to play

Each round hides one entry in a grid of letters. Drag or swipe across neighbouring cells — horizontally, vertically or diagonally — to spell it out. When the word is complete, the dictionary reads its definition back to you.

  • Stage I · The Literate — a 5×5 board. Find the word.
  • Stage II · The Doubter — a 6×6 board. After some words you are shown three definitions; all three are genuine entries, but only one belongs to the word you just found.
  • Stage III · The Accomplice — a 7×7 board. The definitions start watching back.
  • Stage IV · The Author — an 8×8 board, and a second judgment.

Every five different entries you complete strikes one Devil Coin. There are 100 entries and 20 coins in the complete book.

2. My progress disappeared

Progress is stored only on the device you are playing on, in your browser’s local storage or in the app’s own sandbox. It is deliberately not synced anywhere, which means it can be lost by any of the following:

  • Clearing site data or using private browsing on the web
  • Deleting and reinstalling the iOS app
  • Restoring a device from a backup made before you played
  • Pressing RESET MY PROGRESS in the footer — which is permanent and cannot be undone

Unfortunately a lost record cannot be recovered, precisely because nothing is stored on our side. The good news is that nothing was paid for, so nothing has been lost except time.

3. Something looks broken

If a board will not accept a swipe, a definition renders oddly, or the app behaves strangely after an update, tell us what you were doing and what you expected instead. These details help most:

  • Where you were playing — the website or the iOS app, and the app’s version number
  • Your device and operating system version
  • The word you were hunting, if you remember it
  • A screenshot, if the problem is visual

4. An entry got it wrong

Many definitions come from Ambrose Bierce’s The Devil’s Dictionary (1911), which is in the public domain, and the rest were written in that voice for this game. Quotations from the original are reproduced as published, including period spellings and period opinions.

If you spot a factual error, a misattributed quotation, or an entry you think crosses a line, say so. We read and act on these reports; a handful of original Bierce entries were deliberately left out for exactly that reason. We would rather remove a definition than defend one.

5. Accessibility and legibility

The board honours the text size and reduced-motion preferences set on your device, and every control is reachable without a pointer. If you rely on a screen reader or a switch control and hit a wall, describe the wall — this is treated as a bug, not a feature request.

6. What we will never ask for

No one representing this game will ever ask for your password, your card number, a two-factor code, or payment of any kind. There is nothing to buy and no account to secure. Any message asking for those is not from us.

7. Response times

Support is run by one person, so replies are not instant. Expect an answer within a few days, usually sooner. Bug reports that describe a reproducible failure are answered first.

8. Contact

Email support@devildictionary.com — for help, corrections, complaints, or simply to argue with a definition.

If that address is masked by a browser extension or an email-privacy filter, it reads: support at devildictionary dot com.
